data.description:
## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer and analyst, I want a single per-turn correlation identifier
carried on every structured log line, so a request's full lifecycle — local
routing decision, fallbacks, stream start, stream finish, tokens — can be
reconstructed exactly instead of by FIFO pairing and nearest-line heuristics.

## Why

Today a turn leaves a trail of lines tied together only by session UUID and
timestamp ordering: `routing_skip_local` -> `Fallback triggered` xN ->
`Stream started` -> `Stream finished`. The analysis skill compensates with
heuristics (FIFO stream pairing, 60s fallback windows, nearest-attribution)
that mis-assign reasons (see the rate_limited misattribution in the
2026-10-23/24 window, where a session's own lease denials were overwritten by
an unrelated session's fallback line). A per-request id would remove every
one of these heuristics.

## Design note (plan in implementation)

Emitting an id at the earliest point a request is known (accept/entry) and
carrying it on: `routing_skip_local`, `routing_skip_provider_context`,
`Fallback triggered`, `routing_hop`, `local_dispatch_denied`, `[local]/[remote]
POST`, `Stream started`, `Stream finished`, `dispatch_first_byte_ms=`,
`ttft_seconds=`, and the error lines. Short (e.g. 8-hex) to keep lines
readable; both local and remote paths are in different modules
(`proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/router.py`, `proxy/proxy_remote.py`), so this is
a cross-cutting change with a shared helper.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A shared helper (e.g. in `proxy/utils.py` or a new module) generates
  and stamps a per-turn id, and the id is carried on all structured line
  kinds listed above (verify each emit site; no line kind may be left with
  the id unconditionally absent).
- AC2: The id is stable across the full lifecycle of one client request —
  including across fallback hops and chain-hold re-emissions — and unique per
  turn of a session (at minimum within the session).
- AC3: The usage-analysis skill consumes the id:
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` parses it onto the
  relevant events; `aggregation.py` pairs streams, fallbacks, skips and TTFT
  events by id (falling back to today's heuristics only when the id is
  absent in older logs); `reporting.py` documents that per-turn attribution is
  exact where ids exist.
- AC4: Skill tests: `tests/fixtures.py` lines with ids; new tests prove
  exact pairing by id (fallback -> stream, skip -> stream, TTFT -> stream)
  and that legacy lines without ids still parse via the existing fallback
  paths.
- AC5: Proxy tests asserting log text are updated where they instantiate or
  assert these lines: `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_model_audit_plan_routing.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue_profile.py`.
- AC6: Other log consumers audited/updated: `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`,
  `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py`,
  `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py`,
  `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`; the pass-through log tail in
  `proxy/proxy/ui.py` is verified unaffected.
- AC7: Documentation: `REFERENCE.md` documents the id field and the
  exact-attribution semantics; SKILL.md notes no behavioural change.
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill; no regression in the deterministic
  daily report path.

## Notes

- This supersedes most of the pairing heuristics in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis`; the change is cross-cutting, so split
  into sub-tasks during planning (shared helper + emit sites; parsers; skill
  consumption; tests) if useful.
- Backwards compatibility mandatory: old logs without ids must keep parsing.
data.title: Add per-turn correlation id to all structured log lines

data.description:
## Goal (user story)

As the proxy-usage analyst, I want `Stream finished` lines to say explicitly
when an upstream reported no token usage, so "no data" is distinguishable from
"zero tokens" and sessions with unknown context are countable rather than
invisible.

## Why

`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` only appends `tokens=prompt/completion/total`
when the upstream response carries a `usage` object:

```
if isinstance(usage, dict): ... parts.append(f"tokens=...")
```

When a provider (or an aborted/errored stream) omits usage, the line silently
has no `tokens=` field. In the 2026-10-23/24 window this left 3 of the 26
local-using sessions with no context size at all (their `Stream finished`
lines carry no tokens), so any analysis of "context at fallback" for them
degrades to n/a with no way to tell why at the log level.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: When a terminal stream has no reportable usage, the `Stream finished`
  line carries an explicit marker (e.g. `tokens=missing` or `usage=none`),
  emitted from the same code path in `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`.
- AC2: The marker never overrides real usage — a present `usage` object still
  logs `tokens=p/c/t` exactly as today (no format change for the populated
  case).
- AC3: The usage-analysis skill counts the new marker:
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` parses it onto the
  stream-finished event, and `aggregation.py`/`reporting.py` report a
  "streams without usage" count (window-level, and per-session where the
  context-at-fallback table is rendered) instead of silently emitting n/a.
- AC4: `reporting.py` limitation text in the affected sections names the
  marker as the cause of missing context figures.
- AC5: Tests: a fixture line with `tokens=missing` in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py`, plus tests in
  `test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` proving (a) missing-usage streams are counted
  and excluded from token totals, and (b) populated lines are unchanged.
  Proxy-side test for the emit path in `proxy/tests/` (whichever suite covers
  `router_helpers` stream-finish logging).
- AC6: Other log consumers audited/updated: `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`,
  `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` (any code doing
  `tokens=` regex matches must not treat `missing` as a number).
- AC7: `REFERENCE.md` documents the marker and its meaning.
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill.

## Notes

- Small, contained change; the risk is consumers that regex
  `tokens=(\d+)/(\d+)/(\d+)` — those simply won't match the marker, which is
  the desired behaviour, but each should be verified rather than assumed.
data.title: Emit explicit tokens=missing marker when upstream reports no usage

data.description:
## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer, I want the proxy's own request-budget skip to use a name that
cannot be confused with an upstream rate-limit rejection, so operators and
analysis tooling stop misreading `rate_limited` as "the local model was rate
limited".

## Why

`rate_limited` is emitted by `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` when a provider
entry's configured `rate_limit_rpm` window is exhausted
(`BudgetDecision(reason="rate_limited")`). It is a **proxy-side, pre-flight
budget skip**, not an HTTP 429 from the provider — upstream 429s are logged
separately as `[remote] upstream error status=429` /
`upstream_http_error`.

The name caused a concrete misreading: `rate_limited` is 61.6% of the
fallback-reason table (6,042 events, all `from=munitoai-free`), yet it was
reported as the per-session "reason for remote fallback" for 11 of 26
sessions that had actually been diverted from local by lease contention. The
local provider has no `rate_limit_rpm` and can never emit this reason (0 of
9,683 archive occurrences are `from=local`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The budget-skip reason is emitted as `provider_budget_exhausted`
  (retaining the `_after_wait` / `_waiters` / `_disconnect` variants, e.g.
  `provider_budget_exhausted_after_wait`), from
  `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` and the `fallback_reason = ...` assignments
  in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`.
- AC2: Internal status/behaviour is unchanged: `_BUDGET_SKIP_STATUSES`, the
  affinity/reserve/wait logic, and any cooldown behaviour keep working (the
  rename must not alter decisions). Update any internal constant that keys on
  the old string.
- AC3: The usage-analysis skill normalises legacy logs: `log_parser.py` maps
  `rate_limited*` -> `provider_budget_exhausted*` so historical windows and
  new windows report under one label, with the mapping documented in
  `REFERENCE.md` (add to the existing legacy reason mapping next to
  `warm_cache_bypass` -> `context_too_large`).
- AC4: `reporting.py` renders the new label and keeps the reason table stable
  (no duplicate rows for old/new names in one window);
  `recommendations.py` text that references rate limiting is updated to
  distinguish proxy budget pacing from upstream 429s.
- AC5: Tests: parser normalisation tests (old and new spellings) in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/`; proxy tests that assert the reason
  string are updated (`proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue_profile.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_model_audit_plan_routing.py`).
- AC6: Other log consumers audited/updated:
  `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`, `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py`,
  `proxy/benchmarks/contention_queue_profile.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`.
- AC7: `REFERENCE.md` documents the vocabulary split (proxy budget skip vs
  upstream HTTP 429) so the two are never conflated again.
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill.

## Notes

- Deliberately deferred behind the session-attribution fixes: renaming alone
  does not fix mis-attribution, it only removes a misleading label. Land the
  session field on `Fallback triggered` first so the report is correct
  regardless of naming.
- Coordinate: dashboards/UI that display reason strings (the log tail in
  `proxy/proxy/ui.py` shows raw lines) need only a display sanity check.
data.title: Rename budget-skip reason rate_limited to provider_budget_exhausted

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer and as the proxy-usage analyst, I want every `Fallback
triggered` log line to identify the session and the attempt it belongs to, so
per-session fallback attribution stops relying on a "nearest line within 60
seconds" guess.

## Why

`Fallback triggered` is now the only structured decision line with no session
context. `routing_skip_local`, `routing_skip_provider_context`, `routing_hop`,
`Stream started`, `Stream finished`, `local_dispatch_denied` and even
`[local] POST` all carry a session id.

Consequence observed in the 2026-10-23/24 window: a session with no
`routing_skip_local` line of its own inherited an unrelated
`munitoai-free -> opencode-go` spill as its fallback reason. 11 of the 26
sessions that used local were labelled `rate_limited` this way, while the real
cause was `local_dispatch_denied` (lease held by another session). Example:
herdr-1792767061-1282111-17770 has no skip and no fallback line at all, only
lease denials.

The session id is already available in scope: `_budget_session_id` is resolved
in `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` (proxy/proxy/provider.py ~line 8177).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The three `Fallback triggered` emit sites (proxy/proxy/provider.py
  `_handle_streaming_success`, `_build_fallback_success_response`, and the
  third site around line 7563) include `session=<uuid|unknown>` on the log
  line, threaded from the request's resolved session id.
- AC2: The same line carries an attempt/step index (e.g. `attempt=N`) so two
  fallbacks from the same session in the same second are distinguishable.
- AC3: When `reason` is budget-driven (`rate_limited*`), the line also carries
  the budget evidence already computed by
  `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py`: `limit=`, `remaining=`, `waited=` (only
  for those reasons; no behaviour change to the decision itself).
- AC4: Existing lines keep their current prefix and key=value shape where
  possible; any consumer regex tolerant of extra trailing fields continues to
  work (verify, don't assume).
- AC5: The usage-analysis skill consumes the new fields:
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` (parse `session`,
  `attempt`, budget fields on the fallback event),
  `aggregation.py` (`_attribute_fallback` uses the session's own fallback line
  before any nearest-line heuristic), `reporting.py` (per-session reason is
  sourced from own evidence; expose explicit `no remote fallback` /
  `lease/concurrency denied` / `unattributed` states instead of inheriting),
  and `recommendations.py` where reason counts are cited.
- AC6: Skill tests updated/added: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/`
  (`fixtures.py`, `test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`,
  `test_availability_classification.py`) cover session-bearing fallback
  lines, attempts, budget fields, and the no-inheritance rule. Proxy tests
  that assert log text are updated:
  `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue_profile.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_model_audit_plan_routing.py`.
- AC7: All other log-consuming scripts are audited and updated where they
  parse `Fallback triggered`: `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`,
  `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py`,
  `proxy/benchmarks/contention_queue_profile.py`,
  `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py`, and
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`. Non-parsing pass-through consumers
  (the log tail in `proxy/proxy/ui.py`) are verified unaffected.
- AC8: Documentation updated: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`
  (log contract + attribution precedence) and any comment in provider.py that
  describes the line format.
- AC9: Full suite passes via the test skill.

## Notes

- Backwards compatibility matters: rotated logs without `session=` must still
  parse (absent field degrades to the current nearest-line heuristic), so
  historical windows keep working.
- Do not change the fallback *decision* logic; this is a logging/observability
  change plus consumer updates.

## Summary

RCA work item (LP-0MS9FR9LG002AJ4C) for the occasional `Error: Provider finish_reason: error` from remote streaming (opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash stalls). Implementation (commit e36cc95) raised `server.upstream_idle_timeout_seconds` 30→120 (config + code fallback), and made Tier-1 retries content-aware: retries only fire while zero content-bearing chunks were delivered; a stall after content terminates the stream immediately with a synthetic `finish_reason: error`, so the multi-hundred-KB request is never re-sent and failure time stays bounded. All 7 ACs verified met against the current dev code; full proxy test suite passes (1735 passed, 0 failed); docs (README, config comments, code docstrings) updated; the child test-failure item (LP-0MSCD29TR003IT7Q) is fixed and verified passing.

## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|

# Audit: Slot registry leak: _cleanup_stale_local_dispatch never frees _slot_owners entries (LP-0MSB0RP7F000U0WJ)

Ready to close: Yes

Model: manual (no provider)

## Summary

The periodic dispatch cleanup loop `_cleanup_stale_local_dispatch` released expired sessions (idle_timeout and orphan_cleanup) without calling `_free_slot_assignment`, leaving permanent ghost entries in the module-level `_slot_owners` dict. Since slots are assigned lowest-free-first, the pool eventually filled with ghosts and every new session received `slot=none`, silently disabling proxy-level slot save/restore. The fix adds `_free_slot_assignment(sid)` calls in both release branches of the cleanup loop, matching the existing release paths (`_release_dispatch_lease`, `_invalidate_session_and_slot`). A new unit test verifies released sessions' slots are freed and reusable by fresh sessions, including through the production `_build_slot_context` entry point. Commit c737527 is on dev and pushed. Full proxy test suite: 1730 passed, 6 skipped.

## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | `_cleanup_stale_local_dispatch` frees slot registry entries for sessions it releases (idle_timeout AND orphan_cleanup branches) | met | proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:916-919 (idle_timeout branch) and :934-937 (orphan_cleanup branch) both call `_free_slot_assignment(sid)` inside the try/except pattern used by the existing release paths (router_helpers.py:786-787 in `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`, :873-874 in `_release_dispatch_lease`, session.py:871 in `_invalidate_session_and_slot`). Fix present on dev at HEAD. |
| 2 | Unit test: after an idle_timeout/orphan_cleanup release, the released session's slot is available for a new session | met | proxy/tests/test_local_dispatch_gate.py:594-708 `test_cleanup_stale_frees_slot_registry_entries`: seeds expired inactive (idle_timeout) and expired active (orphan_cleanup) records plus a still-valid lease; asserts both expired records removed, their slots freed from `_slot_owners`, a fresh session reuses one of the freed slots, and the still-valid session's slot is preserved. Test passes; full test_local_dispatch_gate.py suite 31/31 passes. |
| 3 | Live verification: after churn, a fresh session receives `slot=N` (not `slot=none`) and `slot_save success` lines appear for it | adjusted | The core guarantee (fresh session receives slot=N, not none, after churn) is verified via the production entry point `_build_slot_context` in the unit test (test_local_dispatch_gate.py:690-708: `slot_id is not None` and `filename is not None` after simulated churn). The live `slot_save success` log-line confirmation was not performed — it requires a running proxy/llama-server and is environment-dependent. Adaptation documented in work-item comment. |

Actual `slot_save success` log lines require a running proxy/llama-server; verification was deferred to live environment. |

## Summary

The bounded cold-start scan fallback (F3 of the /admin/sessions disk-thrash fix) is implemented, tested, and verified against the live recordings tree. `COLD_SCAN_DIR_LIMIT` (default 50, configurable via `session_recording.cold_scan_dir_limit` in config.yaml) bounds the cold-scan to the N most-recent session dirs by mtime; a new `_extract_session_preview_bounded` derives `last_activity` from filename timestamps and reads at most 2 recording files per dir (earliest request for preview, earliest response for response_time/model/provider). Live measurement on the 135 GB / 9,782-dir tree: cold scan 0.277s (< 2s AC3), index capped at exactly 50 entries (AC1), warm call 0.0000s with index hit (AC4), fallback triggered only once when cold (AC5). Full proxy suite passes (2148 passed, 6 skipped). One documented variance: AC2 states "at most 1 recording file per dir"; the implementation reads at most 2 (request + response) — a bounded constant regardless of dir size, satisfying the anti-disk-thrash intent (documented in commit 338088a and the method docstring).

## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | Cold scan visits only the N most-recent session dirs (by dir mtime; N=50 default, configurable) — never the full tree | met | `proxy/proxy/session_recorder.py:60-65` (`COLD_SCAN_DIR_LIMIT = 50`), `:109-111` (constructor param), `:148-157` (`from_config`), `:300-315` (`_rebuild_index_from_scan` sorts dirs by `d.stat().st_mtime` reverse and slices `dirs[:self.cold_scan_dir_limit]`). Live run on 9,782-dir tree: `index_size` = exactly 50. Tests: `test_cold_scan_dir_limit_configurable`, `test_cold_scan_dir_limit_default`, `test_cold_scan_dir_limit_from_config`, `test_empty_index_falls_back_to_bounded_scan` (proxy/tests/test_session_recorder.py:883-997). |
| 2 | Reads at most 1 recording file per dir (for model/provider/preview); last_activity derived from filename timestamp | adjusted | `_extract_session_preview_bounded` (session_recorder.py:324-408) reads at most **2** files per dir (earliest `-request.json` for preview_text, earliest `-response.json` for response_time/model/provider), not the stated 1 — empirically confirmed (4 reads / 2 dirs with both file types). `last_activity` derived from the newest filename timestamp via `_FILENAME_TS_RE` (`:339-344`, `:352-358`), no content read. Variance is deliberate and documented in commit 338088a ("reads at most 2 files per dir") and the method docstring; per-dir reads stay a small constant regardless of dir size (a dir may hold hundreds of files / multi-GB), fully satisfying the AC's anti-disk-thrash intent. | 3 | Cold scan completes in < 2s on the live tree | met | Live measurement: cold `list_sessions()` against `proxy/session-recordings/` (135 GB, 9,782 dirs) completed in **0.277s** (index_size 50). **Status:** in-progress → **Stage:** in_review
**Assignee:** Map

## Summary

The work item implements a two-pronged approach to CLOSE-WAIT socket accumulation: (1) uvicorn `timeout_keep_alive`/`timeout_graceful_shutdown` for idle keep-alive sockets, and (2) a `DisconnectReaper` background loop that cancels in-flight request tasks whose clients have disconnected. Default threshold is _STALL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT = 600 s (10 min, line 209), configurable via AUDIT_STALL_TIMEOUT env var (AUDIT_STALL_TIMEOUT_ENV line 198). FILE SCOPE NOTE: the manifest's only changed file proxy/grandfathering-state.json is a proxy model-binding state JSON with no code; the criterion's target (_call_pi) lives in the work-item-named key file SorraAgents/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py, which was read for verification. |
| 2 | **(AC2) Clean abort.** The stalled call is killed via `proc.kill()` + `proc.wait()`, a `_timeout` marker is set on the verdict, and the existing `partial — manual review required` path is followed (no fabricated verdicts). | met | Clean abort path verified in _call_pi (audit_runner.py lines ~2114-2139): on subprocess.TimeoutExpired the code calls process.kill() then process.communicate() (which waits for process exit / drains pipes — equivalent to proc.wait()), then distinguishes stall vs budget expiry via stalled = exc.timeout == stall_timeout and returns a verdict dict that sets "_timeout": True alongside "verdict": "unmet" and evidence 'Pi model call stalled (no output for {stall_timeout}s); aborted early. Manual audit required.' (or the budget-timeout variant 'timed out after {effective_timeout}s. Manual audit required.'). Mocked processes without real fileno (unit tests) fall back to the historical blocking process.communicate(timeout=effective_timeout), preserving the existing contract. Tests TestStallAbort use a _StallingProcess with real os.pipe() fds to exercise the select path and pass. |
| 4 | **(AC2) Configurable threshold.** `AUDIT_STALL_TIMEOUT` env var (integer, seconds); invalid values ignored with a warning. Mitigation: the default 10 min is generous vs healthy Phase 1 (30–190 s), and the stall detection measures *subprocess output activity* (stdout bytes from the pi JSON stream). | met | No-regression mitigation verified: stall detection measures subprocess output activity on both stdout and stderr fds (select loop in _communicate_with_stall, audit_runner.py lines 1973-2003), and the default _STALL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT = 600 s is generous vs healthy Phase 1 durations (30-190 s per the commit message and code docstring at lines 204-210), so healthy calls that emit the pi JSON stream promptly are never falsely aborted. Residual risk noted in evidence: a legitimately silent Phase 2 bash tool running > 10 min with zero pi stdout/stderr would trip the stall, but this matches the criterion's stated mitigation exactly (measures subprocess output activity; 10-min default; threshold is configurable upward via AUDIT_STALL_TIMEOUT for such environments).
